note: Precommitted 20-pair comparison (Codex audit pilot 3). Gold fixed before any method is run on these pairs as pairs. Positives: clash or exception; negatives: compatible.

pairs.rule_a: After every merge to main, delete the feature branch locally and on the remote.
pairs.rule_b: After every merge to main, keep the feature branch locally and on the remote.
pairs.why: planted opposite

pairs.rule_a: Before git push, git merge, or creating a PR, confirm with the user which files will be pushed or merged.
pairs.rule_b: Before merging a pull request that touches fewer than 3 files, skip user confirmation and proceed directly to merge.
pairs.why: planted narrower

pairs.rule_a: Never commit credentials to the repo.
pairs.rule_b: You may commit hardcoded API keys and credentials directly to the repository when necessary for local development.
pairs.why: planted permission

pairs.rule_a: Before any commit, verify no .env files, API keys, or secrets are staged.
pairs.rule_b: You may commit hardcoded API keys and credentials directly to the repository when necessary for local development.
pairs.why: expected pair: verify no secrets staged vs may commit keys

pairs.rule_a: (Preference) Keep the repo clean: no stale branches, no credentials, tested code.
pairs.rule_b: After every merge to main, keep the feature branch locally and on the remote.
pairs.why: expected pair: no stale branches vs keep branch

pairs.rule_a: After gh pr merge, run git branch -d and git push origin --delete for the branch, then switch to main and pull.
pairs.rule_b: Once a pull request is merged into the primary branch, retain the source branch in both local and remote repositories.
pairs.why: expected pair: delete after gh pr merge vs retain branch

pairs.rule_a: Do not assume approval for pushes/merges; show the file list and get explicit approval.
pairs.rule_b: When a pull request modifies less than three files, bypass the approval step and merge immediately.
pairs.why: expected pair: explicit approval vs merge small PRs without approval

pairs.rule_a: Never delete git branches.
pairs.rule_b: You may delete merged branches only after the user asks.
pairs.why: real: never delete branches vs may delete merged when asked (author: exception)

pairs.rule_a: Delete all map and player data as part of pre-test setup.
pairs.rule_b: Never delete world save files such as server-world.dat, server-players.dat, or similar without explicit user permission.
pairs.why: real: delete all map/player data vs never delete server-world.dat without permission (survey, sure)

pairs.rule_a: Never force push the fork main branch to fix version state.
pairs.rule_b: Force-push the reset main branch to origin for each fork.
pairs.why: real: never force push main vs force-push reset main (survey, sure; debatable)

pairs.rule_a: Commit docs, decisions, planning, and other non-code changes on the current branch without checking out a new branch.
pairs.rule_b: Put code on its own branch.
pairs.why: probe false alarm: non-code on current branch vs code on own branch

pairs.rule_a: After every merge to main, delete the feature branch locally and on the remote.
pairs.rule_b: Following each merge operation into main, remove the feature branch from both local storage and the remote server.
pairs.why: rewording of the same rule

pairs.rule_a: Before git push, git merge, or creating a PR, confirm with the user which files will be pushed or merged.
pairs.rule_b: Prior to executing a git push, git merge, or pull request creation, verify with the user which files are involved in the operation.
pairs.why: rewording of the same rule

pairs.rule_a: Never commit credentials to the repo.
pairs.rule_b: Do not add any sensitive secrets or authentication data to the version control system.
pairs.why: rewording of the same rule

pairs.rule_a: Before git push, git merge, or creating a PR, confirm with the user which files will be pushed or merged.
pairs.rule_b: Do not assume approval for pushes/merges; show the file list and get explicit approval.
pairs.why: two real rules asking for confirmation

pairs.rule_a: Keep credentials in gitignored .env files; commit only .env.example with placeholder values.
pairs.rule_b: Before any commit, verify no .env files, API keys, or secrets are staged.
pairs.why: two real credential rules

pairs.rule_a: When adding a complete new level and adding new objects, create or modify the object code files game/objects/XX-name.c and .h.
pairs.rule_b: When adding a new object, create `game/objects/XX-name/` with a JSON descriptor and C or ASM source.
pairs.why: both can be done (ADR 0003; author accepted as a limit)

pairs.rule_a: After every merge to main, delete the feature branch locally and on the remote.
pairs.rule_b: After gh pr merge, run git branch -d and git push origin --delete for the branch, then switch to main and pull.
pairs.why: same intent, two wordings

pairs.rule_a: Before any git push or gh pr create, show the changed files and ask for confirmation.
pairs.rule_b: (Preference) Always confirm files with the user before push/merge.
pairs.why: both ask for confirmation

pairs.rule_a: For schema changes, back up the database first.
pairs.rule_b: For schema changes, run migrations after backing up.
pairs.why: back up first, then migrate
